name: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder with Anti-Aquaporin-4 Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2015 International Panel for NMO Diagnosis (IPND) Criteria

criteria.description: At least one core clinical characteristic including optic neuritis, acute myelitis, area postrema syndrome, acute brainstem syndrome, symptomatic narcolepsy or acute diencephalic clinical syndrome, or symptomatic cerebral syndrome with MRI lesions
Seropositivity for anti-aquaporin-4 IgG antibodies detected by cell-based assay
Absence of clinical and MRI features typical of multiple sclerosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least one core clinical characteristic plus positive anti-AQP4 antibody serology and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MRI findings supportive but not mandatory if antibody positive

pathognomonic.symptomName: Optic neuritis with severe visual loss
searchTerms: inflammation of optic nerve causing vision loss
optic nerve swelling with vision problems

pathognomonic.notes: Spinal cord lesion extending over three or more vertebral segments
searchTerms: spinal cord swelling over many segments

pathognomonic.symptomName: Area postrema syndrome with intractable hiccups or nausea

common.symptomName: Acute brainstem syndrome with diplopia and dysphagia
searchTerms: brainstem inflammation causing double vision and swallowing problems
acute brainstem symptoms with difficulty swallowing

common.symptomName: Motor weakness or paralysis in limbs
searchTerms: loss of muscle strength in limbs

common.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urinary retention or incontinence
searchTerms: bladder problems like retention or leakage

rare.symptomName: Respiratory failure due to high cervical myelitis
searchTerms: breathing failure from neck spinal cord injury
respiratory arrest due to cervical myelitis
high spinal cord causing breathing problems
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

laboratory: Presence of anti-aquaporin-4 IgG antibodies in serum by cell-based assay
Elevated CSF protein with mild pleocytosis
Negative oligoclonal bands or less frequent than in multiple sclerosis
imaging: MRI showing longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (≥3 vertebral segments)
MRI brain lesions in area postrema or diencephalon
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations under investigation
other: Visual evoked potentials showing delayed conduction
Spinal cord biopsy rarely performed but shows demyelination and necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF
Shorter spinal cord lesions (<3 vertebral segments)
Typical periventricular brain lesions on MRI
Better prognosis and different treatment response

redFlags: Rapid onset of bilateral visual loss
Severe longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis causing paralysis
Intractable hiccups or vomiting indicating area postrema syndrome
references: Wingerchuk DM et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Neurology. 2015.
Jarius S et al. Neuromyelitis optica: clinical features, immunopathogenesis and treatment. Clin Exp Immunol. 2014.
Pittock SJ et al. Neuromyelitis optica and anti-aquaporin-4 antibodies: clinical and therapeutic implications. Lancet Neurol. 2015.
